questions: What does RAG stand for and what does it do in one sentence?
Name the five steps a RAG system uses to answer a question.
Why can a normal AI model give wrong or outdated answers?
Does RAG change the AI model itself? Explain why or why not.
What is a chunk and why is it useful in a RAG system?
correct_answers: RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It helps AI give better answers by first searching documents and using what it finds to write its response.
The five steps are: break documents into chunks, convert chunks into vectors, store vectors in an index, retrieve relevant chunks for the question, generate an answer using those chunks.
A normal AI model is trained on data up to a certain date. It does not know about events after that date or private documents, so it can give outdated or incorrect answers.
No, RAG does not change the AI model. The model's weights stay the same. RAG only gives the model extra text to read at the time of answering.
A chunk is a small piece of a larger document. It is useful because breaking documents into small pieces makes it easier for the system to find the most relevant part to answer a question.
learner_answers: RAG means Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It is when the AI looks up documents before answering, not just from memory.

First you break documents into small pieces called chunks. Then you turn them into vectors. Then you store them in an index. Then when a question comes, you find the relevant chunks. Then the AI uses those chunks to write the answer.
Because it was trained only up to a certain time. After that it does not know new things. Also it does not know private things like your company files.
No it does not change the model. The lesson said the model weights never change. RAG just gives it more text to read when answering.
A chunk is a small part of a document. It helps because then the computer can find just the part that answers your question instead of searching the whole document.
